title: fix: Remove `explicit` from std/boost hash specialisation default constructors
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Remove the `explicit` keyword from the defaulted default constructor of five `std::hash<T>` / `boost::hash<T>` specialisations in `libxrpl`:

- `std::hash<xrpl::MPTID>` (`include/xrpl/protocol/MPTIssue.h`)
- `std::hash<xrpl::MPTIssue>`, `std::hash<xrpl::Asset>` (`include/xrpl/protocol/Book.h`)
- `boost::hash<xrpl::MPTIssue>`, `boost::hash<xrpl::Asset>` (`include/xrpl/protocol/Book.h`)
- `boost::hash<::beast::ip::Address>` (`include/xrpl/beast/net/IPAddress.h`)

No behavioural change; this aligns them with the convention already used by every other hash specialisation in the codebase (`std::hash<xrpl::uint256>`, `std::hash<xrpl::Currency>`, `std::hash<xrpl::NodeID>`, `std::hash<xrpl::Directory>`, `std::hash<xrpl::AccountID>`, and the two `std::hash<xrpl::Issue>` / `std::hash<xrpl::Book>` variants).

### Context of Change

Both `std::hash<T>` and `boost::hash<T>` are required by their respective specifications to satisfy the *Hash* requirements, which include `Cpp17DefaultConstructible`. That requirement mandates the type be default-constructible in copy-initialisation contexts (i.e. `T u{};` and `T v = {};` must be well-formed), not just direct-initialisation.

Marking the defaulted default constructor `explicit` violates this: it makes copy/value-initialisation ill-formed while direct-init (`T{}` as a prvalue expression, `T()` as an operand) still compiles. This is why the bug was latent -- most direct call sites `std::hash<T>{}(x)` are direct-init and work either way. It only bites when a hasher is value-initialised inside a standard/boost library internal that lives in a copy-initialisation context, for example:

- libstdc++'s `_Hashtable_ebo_helper<_Hash>::_M_hash{}` inside a defaulted constructor of `_Hash_code_base`.
- `std::tuple`'s primary constructor evaluating `__is_implicitly_default_constructible_v` on every element, which recursively probes each member via `requires (void(&f)(T)) { f({}); }` (copy-list-

title: fix: Prevent AMM auction slots from being acquired at zero cost when trading fee is zero
body:
<!--
This PR template helps you to write a good pull request description.
Please feel free to include additional useful information even beyond what is requested below.

If your branch is on a personal fork and has a name that allows it to
run CI build/test jobs (e.g. "ci/foo"), remember to rename it BEFORE

the branch after opening the PR will close the PR.
https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-branches-in-your-repository/renaming-a-branch
-->

## High Level Overview of Change
When `sfTradingFee` is 0, `minSlotPrice = lptAMMBalance * 0 / 25 = 0`. An unowned/expired slot can be acquired for `minSlotPrice = 0`, burning zero LP tokens. While the slot provides no immediate benefit (discounted fee is also 0), if the trading fee is later voted up, the slot holder's `sfDiscountedFee` IS updated by AMMVote, so the discount tracks the new fee. However, the slot was acquired for free, meaning there was no economic cost to speculating on future fee increases. The slot holder occupies the slot for 24 hours at zero cost.

title: ci: Do not cache cargo binaries
body:
Swatinem/rust-cache deletes all pre-existing binaries in ~/.cargo/bin when saving the cache, to only cache binaries installed during the job. On persistent self-hosted runners this permanently wipes the cargo tools installed by prepare-runner (cargo-audit, cargo-llvm-cov, cargo-nextest). Set cache-bin: "false" to disable this behavior.

To make it everywhere without too much code/comments duplication, it is refactored into a separate action.

title: build: Sign RPM packages
body:
Nexus cannot sign hosted yum metadata, so the RPMs are signed before upload and clients verify them with gpgcheck=1.

sign_rpm.sh is a separate step that only runs when publishing the RPM leg, so a published RPM is always signed while local, PR and DEB builds need no key. It runs before the artifact upload, so the artifact and the published package are the same bytes.

This doesn't fix rpm upload itself, but should be merged before the fix - let's not have unsigned rpms at all.

body:

-->

## High Level Overview of Change

We don't build nix on macOS in CI:
- Something might fail to build for any new library; after all, a cutting-edge LLVM/Clang on macOS isn't the most common setup.
- It's easy to accidentally break our code.
- Conan packages aren't uploaded, so the initial conan install is always slow.

This PR fixes the problem.
To upload, we need to make sure that libraries/binaries aren't having anything nix-store related, this way they should be use-able with llvm clang even outside nix, and updates to nix flakes (which can easily change paths in nix store) won't break uploaded libraries.

Adding the version from flake.lock to package_id isn't desirable either, because then we'd have to rebuild everything every time it updates.

Converts every `boost::format` call site in the codebase over to `std::format` — 37 sites across 21 files. After this PR, `grep -rn "boost::format\|boost/format" src include` comes back empty. Also fixes three headers that turned out to be relying on `<boost/format.hpp>` arriving transitively.

### Context of Change

`std::format` validates the format string and its arguments **at compile time**. `boost::format` can only report a mismatch by throwing at run time, which for something like `STTx::getMetaSQL` (eight substitutions building a SQL row) means a formatting mistake ships and surfaces in production rather than failing the build.

Most of the conversions are mechanical — `%s`, `%d` and `%c` all become `{}`, and literal braces in `STLedgerEntry::getText` / `STXChainBridge::getText` get doubled:

```cpp
// before
return str(boost::format("{ %s, %s }") % to_string(key_) % STObject::getText());
// after
return std::format("{{ {}, {} }}", to_string(key_), STObject::getText());
```

Three places needed more than a search-and-replace, and they're the ones worth reviewing.

#### `STTx::getMetaSQL` and `Node.cpp` lose their shared `static boost::format` objects

Reusing a `boost::format` instance across calls is not thread-safe, since feeding arguments in with `%` mutates it. `getMetaSQL` had one; `Node.cpp` had four more (`kDeleteLedger`, `kDeleteTranS1`, `kDeleteTranS2`, `kDeleteAcctTrans`) as writable globals touched from `saveValidatedLedger`. They're all plain format-string constants now, with no shared state.

While converting `kDeleteAcctTrans`, note it was formatting a `uint256` through `operator<<`; it now uses the `txnId` string the surrounding loop had already computed.

#### `Node.cpp`'s account-transaction query gets its prefix inlined

This one built its format string by concatenating a `static std::string kPrefix` with a raw literal at run time, which means the string is not a constant and `std::format` can't check it. R

https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-branches-in-your-repository/renaming-a-branch
-->


Pre-ConfidentialKeyRotation, `MPTokenIssuanceSet` rejects any attempt to modify an existing `IssuerEncryptionKey`/`AuditorEncryptionKey`, and an auditor key can never be provided without the issuer key (`temMALFORMED` in preflight).

Post-ConfidentialKeyRotation:
1.  allow late-registering auditor key after issuance key already registered on ledger
2. prevent registering auditor key if issuance key is not already registered or not being registered in the same tx
3. allow late-registering auditor key even if COA > 0
4. allow rotating issuer key even if it already exists on ledger
5. allow rotating auditor key even if it already exists on ledger
6. allow rotating even if COA > 0


Epoch:
1. when not opt-in confidential, epoch absent
2. first time register key: epoch keeps absent, matching issuances whose keys were registered before the ConfidentialKeyRotation amendment.
3. rotating key: epoch + 1
